bespoke_clusters.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: NPS backcountry hydration requires drinking 0.5 to 1 liter of water per hour of strenuous hiking plus electrolytes in warm weather.
core_mechanism_bullets: NPS backcountry hydration requires drinking 0.5 to 1 liter of water per hour of strenuous hiking plus electrolytes in warm weather.
Stopping immediately at the first warm hotspot to apply moleskin prevents friction from shearing skin layers into a fluid blister.
bespoke_clusters.worked_field_example: On a 10-mile summer hike lasting 4 hours at 85 degrees Fahrenheit, each Scout carries at least 3 liters of water and checks heel hotspots at the first 15-minute pack adjustment break.
bespoke_clusters.counselor_tabletop_demo: Cut a donut-shaped moleskin relief pad with medical shears and layer synthetic liner socks under merino wool hiking socks to eliminate heel friction.
bespoke_clusters.real_world_connection_box: NPS Trail Hydration & Blister Prevention Standard: NPS backcountry hydration requires drinking 0.5 to 1 liter of water per hour of strenuous hiking plus electrolytes in warm weather. bespoke_clusters.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Leave No Trace Principle 2 requires walking single-file down the center of established trails to prevent trail widening and erosion.
core_mechanism_bullets: Leave No Trace Principle 2 requires walking single-file down the center of established trails to prevent trail widening and erosion.
Trail right-of-way etiquette requires downhill hikers to yield to uphill hikers, bikers to yield to hikers, and all to yield to horses.
bespoke_clusters.worked_field_example: When encountering horses on a narrow mountain switchback, Scouts step 6 feet off the downhill side of the trail, stand quietly, and speak calmly so the horses know they are human.
bespoke_clusters.counselor_tabletop_demo: Demonstrate single-file trail spacing, uphill right-of-way yielding, and digging a 6-to-8-inch cathole at least 200 feet from water sources.

bespoke_clusters.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Daypack load weight for 10-to-20-mile treks should stay below 15 to 20 percent of body weight with heavy water close to the spine.
core_mechanism_bullets: Daypack load weight for 10-to-20-mile treks should stay below 15 to 20 percent of body weight with heavy water close to the spine.
Proper hiking boot fit leaves a 0.5-inch thumb width in front of the longest toe when laced snugly to prevent downhill toe jamming.
bespoke_clusters.worked_field_example: For a 120-pound Scout tackling a 20-mile hike, total daypack weight including 3 liters of water (6.6 pounds), Ten Essentials, rain shell, and trail food should stay under 18 to 24 pounds.
bespoke_clusters.counselor_tabletop_demo: Pack a daypack with the Ten Essentials, adjust the hip belt to carry 70 percent of the load on the iliac crest, and tie a heel-lock boot lace knot.
